title: Bootstrap VPC module skeletons + repo structure + first example environment
author: Bruno Silva
content:
Title: Bootstrap VPC module skeletons + repo structure + first example environment

Summary
This PR bootstraps the `redwood-terraform` repository layout for the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha). It adds: (1) initial module skeletons (VPC, endpoints, logging, security groups, IAM scaffold placeholders) with consistent naming and conventions, (2) a first runnable example environment (`examples/aws-private-vpc-minimal`) to validate the repo wiring, and (3) baseline CI for terraform fmt/validate plus documentation checks. No production defaults are finalized here; this is the scaffolding to unblock parallel work on module implementations and interface reviews.

Motivation
We’ve had repeated pilot friction in Private deployments caused by inconsistent customer VPC footprints and unclear boundaries between “network foundation” and “installer/cluster”. The alpha effort needs a stable module suite structure and an example that Solutions Engineering can run end-to-end in a sandbox account as a sanity check. This PR focuses on structure and conventions so subsequent PRs can land independently (VPC routing, endpoints, logging, SG patterns, IAM boundaries, integration tests).

What’s included
- Repository structure
  - `modules/` top-level with one directory per module
  - `examples/` with a minimal composition example
  - `docs/` for alpha-specific architecture notes + module interface conventions
  - `scripts/` for local lint/validate helpers
- Module skeletons (placeholders + interface stubs)
  - `modules/vpc/` (CIDR, subnets, tags; stub outputs)
  - `modules/vpc_endpoints/` (interface placeholder; no endpoints created yet)
  - `modules/logging/` (flow logs placeholder; destination to be implemented)
  - `modules/security_groups/` (naming conventions + stub SG outputs)
  - `modules/iam_installer/` (placeholder role + trust policy stub; no permissions finalized)
- Example environment
  - `examples/aws-private-vpc-minimal/` composes modules with minimal variables and produces outputs expected by the installer later (VPC ID, private subnet IDs, endpoint security group ID placeholder)
- Conventions
  - Standard variable naming (`name`, `environment`, `tags`) across modules
  - Required `README.md` per module with: purpose, inputs, outputs, non-goals, and extension points
  - `versions.tf` placeholder, provider constraints to be pinned in follow-up PR
- CI baseline
  - GitHub Actions workflow for `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` (examples only for now)
  - Docs check: ensure each module has a README and `variables.tf`/`outputs.tf`

Out of scope
- No AWS resources beyond the example’s minimal VPC wiring are finalized here
- No endpoint catalog decisions (ECR/S3/STS/Logs) yet
- No logging retention defaults or SIEM hooks yet
- No opinionated SG rules (ingress/egress) beyond naming conventions
- No release/versioning automation

Notes on module boundaries (alpha direction)
This PR reflects a draft boundary that we should confirm in ENG-4829:
- `modules/vpc`: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT strategy (later PR)
- `modules/vpc_endpoints`: interface endpoints + gateway endpoints + private DNS toggles (later PR)
- `modules/logging`: VPC Flow Logs and log destinations (later PR)
- `modules/security_groups`: a small set of opinionated SGs intended to be composed (later PR)
- `modules/iam_installer`: scaffolding for an installer execution role with optional permission boundaries (later PR)
The example composes these modules but keeps the placeholders explicit to avoid implying defaults are decided.

Changed areas (high level)
- modules/vpc/*
- modules/vpc_endpoints/*
- modules/logging/*
- modules/security_groups/*
- modules/iam_installer/*
- examples/aws-private-vpc-minimal/*
- docs/conventions.md
- .github/workflows/terraform.yml
- scripts/tf.sh

Commits
- bootstrap: add repo skeleton + module directories
- docs: add module README template + conventions doc
- examples: add aws-private-vpc-minimal example
- ci: add terraform fmt/validate workflow

How to test
- From `examples/aws-private-vpc-minimal`:
  - `terraform init`
  - `terraform fmt -check`
  - `terraform validate`
  - (optional) `terraform plan` with a throwaway AWS account/credentials

Review notes / open questions
- Naming: should modules be prefixed `aws_` (e.g., `aws_vpc`) or keep provider-agnostic names with AWS scope stated in README?
- Outputs: which outputs are required for the installer integration (e.g., endpoints, log destinations)? This PR only stubs them.
- Example directory layout: is the example closer to what SE/PS expects for pilots?

---

Conversation

Irene Choi (review): The structure looks good. Please keep module interfaces minimal until we lock ENG-4829. Two requests: (1) add a root-level `CONTRIBUTING.md` with basic workflow (fmt/validate), (2) ensure each module has consistent variable names (`name`, `tags`, `environment`). Also, can we avoid committing provider version constraints until Sahana weighs in?

Bruno Silva (author): Ack on both. I’ll add CONTRIBUTING and normalize variable naming. Provider pins will come in a separate PR once we align on versions.

Victor Alvarez (review): On boundaries: I’d prefer `modules/vpc` includes route tables/NAT because otherwise customers wire it wrong. But agree we shouldn’t finalize defaults here. Suggest adding a short “module responsibilities” section in each README so it’s clear what is intentionally omitted.

Bruno Silva (author): Good call. Added “Responsibilities / Non-goals” to each module README and called out that routing/NAT defaults are TBD.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI workflow: can we run `terraform validate` for modules too? Even if they don’t create resources, we can at least validate syntax. Also, add a step to verify `README.md` exists per module (you mentioned it; I don’t see enforcement yet).

Bruno Silva (author): Updated workflow to validate modules (where init/validate is safe) and added a small script to fail if README is missing.

Hanae Suzuki (review): Security nit: please avoid any default that implies public exposure. In the example, make sure subnets are clearly labeled private/public and we don’t accidentally attach an IGW to the “private” route table. Also, for IAM placeholder, avoid granting any wildcard permissions even in examples.

Bruno Silva (author): Updated the example to clearly separate public vs private route tables (private remains placeholder until NAT work lands) and kept IAM module as a non-functional scaffold (no permissions attached).

Markus Klein (review): From field POV, examples matter. Can we add a `examples/README.md` that states “alpha / not supported” and tells SE what inputs they typically need (CIDR, AZs, tags)? Also, please add outputs in the example that match what the installer will likely ask for so we can start building a checklist.

Bruno Silva (author): Added `examples/README.md` with alpha disclaimer and typical inputs. Also added placeholder outputs with comments that they’ll be wired to installer preflight expectations later.

Connor O'Brien (review): Request: add a `CHANGELOG.md` placeholder and note that semver/release process is coming later. Helps set expectations.

Bruno Silva (author): Added `CHANGELOG.md` placeholder + note in root README.

CI
- terraform-fmt: pass
- terraform-validate (modules + examples): pass
- docs/checks: pass

Merge
- Squash merged by Irene Choi on 2025-05-23

Post-merge follow-ups
- ENG-4829: lock module interfaces + required outputs
- Next PRs: VPC routing/NAT defaults, endpoints module implementation, logging defaults, IAM boundary design, integration test harness
